pairs.question: Utrum lux proprie in spiritualibus dicatur?
pairs.answer: Si autem accipiatur secundum quod est in usu loquentium ad omnem manifestationem extensum, sic proprie in spiritualibus dicitur.
pairs.derivation: The article's disputed question (Utrum...) is the genuine interrogative; the author answers it in the Respondeo (the 'ARTICULUS 1' header is dropped). The Respondeo opens with a long non-answering preamble distinguishing a name's primary imposition from its usage and illustrating with 'visio' ('Respondeo dicendum quod de aliquo nomine dupliciter convenit loqui... Deum videbunt.'), then applies it to 'lux'. I advance the answer start past the preceding conditional ('Si ergo accipiatur nomen luminis secundum suam primam impositionem, metaphorice in spiritualibus dicitur, ut Ambrosius dicit.', which gives only the metaphorical horn) to the operative concluding sentence affirming the question's 'proprie': taken as extended in usage to every manifestation, light is properly said of spiritual things. Nothing follows it in the Respondeo body before 'Et per hoc patet responsio ad obiecta.'

pairs.question: Utrum lux sit corpus?
pairs.answer: Respondeo dicendum quod impossibile est lumen esse corpus.
pairs.derivation: Article-level disputed question answered by the author (the 'ARTICULUS 2' header is dropped). The Respondeo opens with the direct answer itself, so no preamble needs skipping; I keep the full opening sentence stating light cannot be a body. Stopped at its full stop, before 'Quod quidem apparet tripliciter.' which begins the threefold proof.

pairs.question: Utrum lux sit qualitas?
pairs.answer: Dicendum est ergo quod, sicut calor est qualitas activa consequens formam substantialem ignis, ita lux est qualitas activa consequens formam substantialem solis, vel cuiuscumque alterius corporis a se lucentis, si aliquod aliud tale est.
pairs.derivation: Article-level disputed question answered by the author (the 'ARTICULUS 3' header is dropped). The Respondeo opens with a non-answering preamble reporting and refuting two prior opinions ('Respondeo dicendum quod quidam dixerunt quod lumen in aere non habet esse naturale... Alii vero dixerunt quod lux est forma substantialis solis... Unde non potest esse forma substantialis solis.'). I advance the answer start to the operative determinative sentence 'Dicendum est ergo quod... si aliquod aliud tale est.', which affirms that light is an active quality following the substantial form of the sun. Stopped at its full stop, before the corroborating 'Cuius signum est, quod radii diversarum stellarum habent diversos effectus...'.

pairs.question: Utrum convenienter lucis productio in prima die ponatur?
pairs.answer: Ergo oportuit lucem fieri prima die.
pairs.derivation: Article-level disputed question answered by the author (the 'ARTICULUS 4' header is dropped). The Respondeo is a very long survey of opinions (Augustine, Basil, Chrysostom) on whether light here means spiritual creation, never giving a single clean answering sentence to the fittingness question. The cleanest direct answer is the Sed contra's concluding sentence 'Ergo oportuit lucem fieri prima die.', which states the answer (light fittingly produced on the first day). Window is the single answering sentence; the preceding premises of the Sed contra ('id sine quo non potest esse dies, oportuit fieri in prima die. Sed sine luce non potest esse dies.') are the supporting argument, omitted.
